exact_excerpts.text: For the raw walker, undefined continues without a direct replacement; false on enter skips that node's descendants and its leave callback; BREAK is an identity sentinel that exits the whole walk without unwinding ancestor leave callbacks. Other defined results record an edit. An AST-node replacement on enter supplies the children subsequently traversed, without another enter callback for the replacement itself; a non-node result, including null, prevents descent. False on leave is not recorded as a replacement (src/language/visitor.ts:100-101,329-380).

Composition preselects handlers by kind and invokes active visitors in input-array order on both enter and leave; leave order is not reversed. Each callback retains its original visitor as this. Enter false records the current node as that visitor's skip marker, suppressing its descendant callbacks and its own leave callback, then normally clearing the marker when that node is left. BREAK permanently disables only that visitor. Neither signal is forwarded as a global traversal instruction. Leave false is absorbed, so later visitors still run (src/language/visitor.ts:423-475). Separate full-document passes would instead have pass-major ordering; consolidating them can therefore change side-effect and error ordering even when they do not edit.

criteria.reason: The answer distinguishes direct-walk termination from permanently disabling a single composed visitor. Its general composed BREAK statement covers enter and leave. Source branches at visitor.ts340-342,453-454,466-467 implement exactly that distinction.

exact_excerpts.text: Edits returned through visit use copied arrays and objects as changes propagate upward. Null removes array entries, with offsets accounting for earlier removals; object child properties receive null directly. Leave callbacks see nodes incorporating completed child edits. The walker returns its resulting root rather than mutating the original through this edit mechanism; direct mutation inside callbacks is not prevented (src/language/visitor.ts:287-319,349-365,382-387).

Editing is a shared control effect: the first defined result other than false or BREAK immediately returns from the composition callback, suppressing remaining visitors for that phase. An enter replacement therefore prevents later visitors from entering either the original node or its replacement, although active visitors can subsequently see replacement descendants and its leave event. Null removal suppresses later enter callbacks and all traversal of that subtree. A leave edit similarly suppresses remaining leave callbacks. This differs from independent passes over either the original document or successively transformed documents (src/language/visitor.ts:446-475,349-359,367-378).

exact_excerpts.text: Compatibility assessment: both validation paths already compose rule visitors into one outer AST walk. Executable validation uses visitWithTypeInfo(typeInfo, visitInParallel(...)); SDL validation uses visitInParallel directly (src/validation/validate.ts:171-181,193-209). A simple loop forwarding each handler's result to visit would change behavior: skip and break must remain local to each constituent visitor. Even the existing composition does not provide isolated editing passes.

Executable-validation integration must preserve validate's optional diagnostic tracing, default rule list, schema assertion, shared ValidationContext and TypeInfo, and options. Its traversal excludes description children. Errors are reported through context.reportError, which invokes the configured error callback; they are not collected from visitor return values. The default maximum is 100, and an additional report after reaching the limit throws a sentinel that is appended to the returned errors. The walk also catches validationAbortedError by identity and rethrows other exceptions; rule construction occurs before that try block (src/validation/validate.ts:48-57,129-189; src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:77-79).

exact_excerpts.text: Traversal and ordering: visit performs depth-first traversal, calls enter before children and leave afterward, processes arrays in index order, and selects child properties from visitorKeys, defaulting to QueryDocumentKeys. Arrays themselves receive no visitor callback. Callbacks receive node, key, parent, path, and ancestors with the visitor as this (src/language/visitor.ts:261-338,367-380; src/language/ast.ts:247-290). visitInParallel invokes active visitors in input order on both enter and leave; leave order is not reversed, and each callback's this is its original visitor (src/language/visitor.ts:434-475).

Handler selection must remain consistent. A kind-specific object supplies that kind's enter/leave handlers; a kind-specific function supplies enter only. Generic enter/leave handlers are used only when neither kind-specific form applies, so a missing phase in a kind-specific handler does not fall back to the generic phase (src/language/visitor.ts:499-517). visit resolves handlers before walking, and visitInParallel builds per-kind handler arrays when composing (src/language/visitor.ts:266-269,429-439). A replacement that resolves mutable visitor properties on every event could change behavior.

exact_excerpts.text: Type tracking must surround the combined visitor. visitWithTypeInfo enters the original node before dispatch. For any defined enter result, it leaves the original node and enters the replacement only if isNode accepts it. Wrapping every rule independently around the same TypeInfo would apply multiple stack transitions per node. Regression checks must cover skips, removal, replacement across node kinds, and type information observed by remaining visitors.

exact_excerpts.text: Direct visit control signals differ from composed signals. undefined means no callback edit. false on enter skips the subtree and its leave callback; false on leave does not initiate skipping or record a replacement. Identity equality with BREAK stops the entire direct walk. Other defined values are edits, including null. In visitInParallel, enter false instead records that visitor's current node as a skip marker while other visitors continue. Its matching leave resets the marker without invoking that visitor's leave callback. BREAK from either phase permanently disables only that visitor for the composite's lifetime; it is consumed rather than forwarded to the walker. false on composed leave is also consumed. exact_excerpts.text: Edits are shared traversal effects, not isolated per-pass transformations. On either phase, the first composed callback returning a defined value other than false or BREAK immediately returns that value to visit, preventing later visitors from receiving that same node event. Even returning the original node object takes this branch. An AST replacement returned on enter is traversed through its children without another enter event for the replacement itself; its leave event can reach later visitors. A null or other non-node enter replacement skips children and leave entirely. A leave replacement is not subsequently traversed. Thus neither continuing dispatch on the original node nor piping the replacement through remaining callbacks preserves current behavior. Sources: src/language/visitor.ts:334-360,370-378,446-475.

The walker applies edits by copying changed arrays and objects. null removes an array element, with offsets adjusted for subsequent removals; an object property edit assigns null rather than deleting the property. Child edits are assembled before the parent's leave callback. The walker returns the original root when no edits remain, or its recorded replacement otherwise. These copy operations do not protect against callbacks directly mutating input objects. Sources: src/language/visitor.ts:287-319,349-364,382-387.

criteria.reason: The answer correctly identifies first-edit short circuiting on either phase, later visitors missing that event, and replacement children being traversed without redispatching enter. exact_excerpts.text: Handler selection gives a kind-specific object precedence over generic enter/leave handlers. A kind-specific function supplies only enter, without falling back to a generic leave. Generic handlers apply when neither supported kind-specific form is present. visit and visitInParallel resolve handlers for all known kinds before traversal; dynamically changing visitor properties during traversal therefore does not update these cached selections. Callback this is the visitor object, including each original visitor inside composition. Sources: src/language/visitor.ts:266-269,334-338,429-438,450,465,499-518.

The walker performs depth-first traversal: enter precedes children and leave follows them. Child property order follows the supplied visitor-key map, defaulting to QueryDocumentKeys, and arrays are traversed in index order without invoking callbacks on the arrays themselves. Callbacks receive node, key, parent, path and ancestors. Both composed enter and composed leave dispatch visitors in their original array order; leave order is not reversed. Sources: src/language/visitor.ts:261-265,284-338,367-380,446-475; src/language/ast.ts:247-305.

exact_excerpts.text: The type-aware wrapper must remain outside the composed visitor. It enters TypeInfo before dispatch, so callbacks see the current node's type state. When enter returns any defined result, it leaves the original node immediately and enters the result only if it is an AST node. On normal leave it dispatches callbacks before leaving TypeInfo. Because the composer consumes individual false and BREAK signals, those signals do not unwind the shared type state while other rules continue. Reordering these layers or independently updating the same TypeInfo for every rule would change behavior. Sources: src/utilities/TypeInfo.ts:936-967; src/validation/validate.ts:157-180.

exact_excerpts.text: Compatibility assessment: executable-document and SDL validation already compose rules into a shared walk. validateImpl uses visit(documentAST, visitWithTypeInfo(typeInfo, visitInParallel(ruleVisitors)), filteredKeys); validateSDL uses visit(documentAST, visitInParallel(ruleVisitors)). A straightforward loop that merely invokes every visitor would lose existing independent skip/stop handling and edit arbitration. Consolidating separate full-document passes would also change observable scheduling from pass-by-pass to node-by-node, so arbitrary stateful passes are not automatically equivalent.
